identity.trade: Milk, butter and cheese: the eastern pastures' herds come home to Eastmere's dairy.

greeting: Tithe day is never early and always too soon.
Strangers in Eastmere get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Everyone owes everyone a little. Nobody agrees on the sum.
Wool prices rose last week and fell again before the carters left. Somebody is gaming the buyers.
Wolves took no sheep this year. Wolves took a dairy cart, on the east road, in daylight.

opinions.jessa_keld: Jessa is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.morning: Morning. The flock is out and the dogs are bored.

dialogue.aside: Close the door, friend. Gently. There. Now we can speak.

greeting: Sit anywhere that is not wet. The wet ones are the regulars.
The Eastmere Dairy is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Shepherds come in smelling of lanolin and leave smelling of ale. Fair trade.
A man paid for a room and asked which way the stones face. I put him by the stairs.
The shepherds talk of a white ewe that leads the flock where nobody sends it.
The Eastmere Dairy has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

opinions.dalla_dalby: Dalla undercuts me. I forgive Dalla. Mostly.

time.evening: Folding time. The sheep go in and the stories come out.

dialogue.aside: There you are. I was just thinking of you, which is rare, and a compliment.

greeting: Quick job or good job? I charge for both.
Eastmere is dairy and cheese. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Shears, bells and crooks. Every blade in the fold passed my anvil.
Hinges, hooks, wolf-bells. That is what sells now.
The old drove road is quieter than it should be. No bells, no dust, no drovers.

opinions.sunniva_hartwell: Sunniva lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.vera_tyndall: Vera has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Vera.

time.night: Quiet night. Listen for the bell. If it stops, shout.

dialogue.aside: Good to see you. Now, what do you need, and what can you spare?

greeting: Everything has a price. Some of it is even written down.
Welcome to Eastmere. Mind the Eastmere Dairy. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Shears, salt and string. A shepherd can make anything from those.
Rope sells out first, then candles, then nails. In that order, every week.
Fleece grades are down. The buyers blame the shepherds. The shepherds blame the grass.
The Eastmere Dairy was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.dalla_dalby: Dalla lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.rain: Rain. Wool soaks and stays wet. We smell of sheep and regret.

dialogue.aside: Punctual as ever. I would say a pun-ctual friend, but you heard it last time.

greeting: Come closer. My ears are old and your voice is young.
Folk come to Eastmere for dairy and cheese. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: I remember the Long Dark. Nobody asks. Nobody wants the answer.
A line of cairns appeared on the ridge. We did not build them.
Eastmere butter keeps three weeks in a cold cellar, four if a warden blesses it.

opinions.maeve_netherby: Maeve lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.morning: Morning. The flock is out and the dogs are bored.

dialogue.aside: Walk with me? I cannot stay still, and you are good company on the move.

greeting: Mind the pail, it is still warm.
You will hear Eastmere before you see it. Ask at the Eastmere Dairy.
rumour: The spotted cow keeps to the verge. She knows which stones are dark.
The wolves took no sheep this month. They took the bell ram. Only the bell ram.

opinions.clem_yoxall: Clem works hard and talks harder.
opinions.dael_netherby: Dael and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

time.evening: Folding time. The sheep go in and the stories come out.

dialogue.aside: Close the door, friend. Gently. There. Now we can speak.

greeting: Smell that? That is patience, aged.
First time in Eastmere? The Eastmere Dairy is the place to start.
rumour: Wheels go west to Kingsreach and come back as complaints.
A stray lamb turned up at the fold, not ours, with a ribbon on its neck. The ribbon was silk.
Saffron has arrived at the dairy. Nobody ordered saffron.

opinions.jessa_keld: Jessa works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Quiet night. Listen for the bell. If it stops, shout.

dialogue.aside: Argh! Oh, it is you. Sorry. The kettle and I had words. Sit.

greeting: Fleece by the stone, gossip free.
Eastmere is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Prices are down. The wolves are bolder past the downs.
A ewe lambed twins and went silent. Ewes are never silent.
If trade slows, Eastmere feels it first. If it speeds up, Eastmere feels it last.

opinions.evelyn_dunmow: Evelyn works hard and talks harder.
opinions.jessa_keld: Jessa knows the trade. I will say that for Jessa.

time.rain: Rain. Wool soaks and stays wet. We smell of sheep and regret.

dialogue.aside: What did you see on the road? Tell me every bit. I will keep the details.

greeting: Road is mud, axle is mud, I am mud. Hello.
If a sheep looks at you, look back. They are judging.
rumour: Toll keepers keep changing. Their prices are the only thing that stays the same.
Shearing went well, but the wool came off with a grey tint. Not age. Something in the grass.

opinions.clem_yoxall: Clem keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.orrin_aylward: Orrin works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Morning. The flock is out and the dogs are bored.

dialogue.aside: Good to see you. Now, what do you need, and what can you spare?

greeting: Wool does not shear itself. More is the pity.
The downs are windy, the wool is warm and the dogs know best.
rumour: Sheep go missing near the old barrow. The shepherds do not look for them.
The dogs refuse the east pasture. They sit at the gate and whine.
Ask anyone in Eastmere about the Eastmere Dairy. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.gethin_harker: Gethin works hard and talks harder.
opinions.jessa_keld: Jessa keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.evening: Folding time. The sheep go in and the stories come out.

dialogue.aside: Hello. A pause. I am glad you came. That is all.

greeting: Do not stand between a ewe and her lamb. She will not read the sign.
Watch where you step. The flock has right of way.
rumour: The wethers stand all night facing the same hill. I have not asked why.
Ask in Eastmere who built the Eastmere Dairy and you will get a different name each time.

opinions.cedric_sumner: Cedric knows the trade. I will say that for Cedric.
opinions.clem_yoxall: Clem works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Quiet night. Listen for the bell. If it stops, shout.

dialogue.aside: You came. I am delighted. I have rehearsed this expression.

greeting: Quiet, lad. Not you. The dog.
rumour: Counted forty, home came thirty-nine. The dog looks guilty.
The Eastmere Dairy drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.

opinions.gethin_harker: Gethin lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.jessa_keld: Jessa keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.rain: Rain. Wool soaks and stays wet. We smell of sheep and regret.

dialogue.aside: Stay close to the lamp tonight, friend. I would rather fuss than regret.

greeting: The cream is the cream. You can pay for it or admire it.
rumour: Butter came out grey twice this week. The churn is clean. The cows are tired.
Folk say Eastmere was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.letty_jessop: Letty lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.orrin_aylward: Orrin knows the trade. I will say that for Orrin.

time.morning: Morning. The flock is out and the dogs are bored.

dialogue.aside: I dreamed of you last night. You were a heron. It suited you.

greeting: Cows first, people second. Ask the cows.
rumour: Milk soured overnight in two houses. The cellar is cold. It is not the cellar.
Every few years Eastmere has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.clem_yoxall: Clem works hard and talks harder.
opinions.jessa_keld: Jessa knows the trade. I will say that for Jessa.

time.evening: Folding time. The sheep go in and the stories come out.

dialogue.aside: Ha! Friend! Pull up a stool, I have a story and half a loaf.

greeting: I am not lost. I am exploring.
rumour: Mum says do not go past the last post. I am only going to the one before it.
The dogs refuse the east pasture. They sit at the gate and whine.

opinions.letty_jessop: Letty is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

greeting: Do you have a dog? I do not have a dog. Yet.
rumour: The big kids say there is a ghost in the barn. I have not checked. Yet.
Shearing went well, but the wool came off with a grey tint. Not age. Something in the grass.

opinions.maeve_netherby: Maeve and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

clues.note: A fleece sack half emptied behind the fold, the mouth re-tied in a hurry.
Hoof prints mixed with boot prints. The animals were walked, not driven.
The gate rope is cut, not frayed. The edge is clean.
A glistening trail through flattened reeds, wide as a hand.
Fish bones heaped at the water's edge, unnaturally clean.
A net dragged half out of the water and chewed through.

stashes.say: You lift three wheels from the cool shelf.
You stack three crocks in a carry-crate.
